required_elements: Panic Attacks and Diaphragmatic Breathing
During a panic attack, hyperventilation leads to low blood CO2, causing cerebral vasoconstriction and alkalosis
This exacerbates dizziness, paresthesia, and a sense of impending doom, creating a vicious cycle
Diaphragmatic breathing technique: Exhale slowly through the mouth; visualize breathing in calmness and breathing out tension; this reduces sympathetic nervous system activation
This technique is suitable as a non-pharmacological intervention before or in the early stages of a panic attack but does not constitute a complete treatment
Self-assessment: If panic attacks are frequent and significantly impair daily life (e.g., agoraphobic avoidance), seek medical evaluation

The 7 items: nervousness, worry, restlessness, trouble relaxing, being so restless it is hard to sit still, becoming easily annoyed or irritable, feeling afraid something awful might happen

GAD-7 is only a self-report screening tool; it cannot replace a professional diagnosis; high scores warrant clinical evaluation

required_elements: Androgenetic Alopecia (AGA)
Key mechanism: Testosterone is converted to dihydrotestosterone by the action of type II 5α-reductase
DHT binds to androgen receptors on hair follicles, initiating a signaling cascade
This shortens the anagen phase of the hair cycle and causes follicular miniaturization (terminal follicles transform into vellus follicles)
Hair loss predominantly affects the vertex and frontal scalp; occipital follicles are not DHT-sensitive

required_elements: Urticaria and Mast Cells
High-affinity IgE receptors on the mast cell surface cross-link, triggering degranulation and release of preformed mediators such as histamine
Histamine binds to H1 receptors on dermal blood vessels → vasodilation, increased vascular permeability → wheal formation
Pruritus is elicited by histamine stimulating C-nerve fiber endings
Oral antihistamines relieve symptoms by blocking H1 receptors

required_elements: Hand Dermatitis Prevention
Handwashing tips: Use lukewarm water rather than excessively cold or hot water; wash gently
Use mild hand cleansers; avoid products with high concentrations of alkaline soap bases
Core principle: Immediately pat hands dry after washing (without rubbing) and apply a thick layer of hand cream/moisturizer
Those who do housework or wash hands frequently should use a protective hand cream containing ceramides or petrolatum
